info.description: Imports an export text (or a bare workflow document). With `check: true` it only reports the workflows, names that clash, and how each connection, persona and project they need stands here (found, missing, kind_mismatch). Then `mapping` maps each missing one to a local name (a project key to a local project's key or id) or null to leave it unmapped, and `targets` (one per workflow, in order) give scope/projectId and, on a name clash, `copy` or `versionOf` (a proposed version). New workflows start disabled. The user confirms each call.

ImportMapping.description:
The user's answers for what is not found: each name (a connection's or persona's as the documents have it, a
project's key) to a local one, or null to leave it unmapped. A name that is found needs no entry; one given anyway
is used.

versionOf.description: Import as a new version of this workflow (never a repo one).

Every project's, narrowed by its triggers' `projects`.
Not about a code project (manual and scheduled triggers).

info.title: Message a session

tools.does: Read a pull request with its comments and reviews

info.description: The session's pull request (or one by number or branch) on the project's forge: its state, whether it can merge, and every comment and review by the repository's collaborators (others' are left out: `leftOut` counts them). Review comments have an id to answer with `change_request_comment`'s `replyTo`.

branch.description: A branch whose pull request to show, instead of the session's.

number.description: The pull request's number; the session's branch's when left out.

info.name: change_request_view
info.title: View the pull request

tools.does: Comment on a pull request or answer a review comment

info.description: Adds a comment to the session's pull request (or one by number), or with `replyTo` answers a review comment in its thread. It is posted as the user's GitHub login.

number.description: The pull request's number; the session's branch's when left out.

replyTo.description:
A review comment's id (`change_request_view`): the comment answers it in its thread instead of going on the
conversation.

info.name: change_request_comment
info.title: Comment on the pull request

tools.does: Open a pull request for the session's branch

info.description: Opens a pull request from the session's branch (push it first) into the ticket attempt's base branch, or `base`, with a title and a Markdown body; `draft` opens it as a draft. A branch that already has an open one gets that one back. It is opened as the user's GitHub login.

base.description: The branch it merges into; the ticket attempt's base when left out.

body.description: Markdown: what changed and why, and how it was checked.

info.name: change_request_open
info.title: Open a pull request

tools.does: Ask again for the merge of the session's pull request after the merge queue dropped it

info.description: Sets the session's ticket attempt's pull request to merge again (auto-merge, or back into the merge queue) once you have fixed and pushed what made it drop out. Only for a pull request that was already set to merge: the user or the project's workflow decides the first merge. The project's merge policy applies (it may wait for CI on the push).
info.name: change_request_merge
info.title: Merge the pull request again

tools.does: Read a branch's CI runs

info.description: The recent CI runs on the session's branch (or another): each run's workflow, state, commit and URL, and the failed jobs of failed runs. `ci_failed_logs` reads their logs.

branch.description: The branch; the session's when left out.

info.name: ci_runs
info.title: CI runs

tools.does: Read the logs of a CI run's failed jobs

info.description: The failed jobs of a CI run (by id, else the newest failed run on the session's branch), each with the end of its log: what to fix.

runId.description: A run's id (`ci_runs`); the newest failed run on the session's branch when left out.

info.name: ci_failed_logs
info.title: Failed CI logs

tools.does: Read an issue and its comments

info.description: An issue of the project's repository on its forge: title, description, labels, state and comments.
info.name: issue_view
info.title: View an issue

tools.does: Comment on an issue

info.description: Adds a comment to an issue of the project's repository, posted as the user's forge login.
info.name: issue_comment
info.title: Comment on an issue

tools.does: Report a bug in PDT (an issue on its repository, or a local ticket)

info.description: Reports a bug in PDT itself (not in the project you work on), as Host settings route it: an issue on PDT's GitHub repository, or a Draft bug ticket on the instance PDT is developed on. includeDiagnostics adds this instance's version, OS, update state and the end of its log, redacted. The user confirms each call.

description.description: What happened, what you expected, and how to make it happen again (Markdown).

includeDiagnostics.description: Add this instance's diagnostics (version, OS, update state, the end of the pdtd log), redacted.

title.description: One line saying what went wrong.

info.name: report_bug
info.title: Report a bug in PDT

tools.does: Look at the Discord server: its channels and webhooks

info.description: The Discord server a bot connection manages: its categories, channels and webhooks (with the connection each webhook is saved as), and whether you may change it without asking.

connection.description: A Discord bot connection's name; the only one when left out.

info.name: discord_get
info.title: Look at the Discord server

tools.does: Create, rename, move or archive Discord channels

info.description: Creates, renames, moves or archives (moves into Archive) channels and categories on the Discord server, in order. The user confirms each call unless the bot connection lets you act.

Change.description: One change `discord_change` makes. Channels and categories are named by id, name or `#name`.

oneOf.description: A new channel or category.

category.description: The category to put it in (not for a category).

kind.description: text (the default), category, voice, announcement or forum.

oneOf.description: Renames a channel or category.
Moves a channel into a category; out of any when `category` is left out.
Moves a channel into the Archive category (made when missing). Nothing is deleted.

ChannelKind.description: What a channel is (Discord's channel types, the ones a server has).

changes.description: Made in order; the first that fails stops the rest.

connection.description: A Discord bot connection's name; the only one when left out.

info.name: discord_change
info.title: Change the Discord server

tools.does: Make a Discord webhook for discord.post steps

info.description: Makes a webhook on a channel (and the channel, with createChannel) and saves it as a discord_webhook connection that discord.post steps use by name. Its URL is never shown. The user confirms each call unless the bot connection lets you act.

category.description: A new channel's category (made when missing).

connection.description: A Discord bot connection's name; the only one when left out.

createChannel.description: Make the channel (a text channel) when the server has none called that.

name.description: The new `discord_webhook` connection's name, which `discord.post` steps use (`briefs`).

webhookName.description: The webhook's name in Discord (shown as the sender); the connection's name when left out.

info.name: discord_webhook
info.title: Make a Discord webhook

tools.does: Browse the Scryer media library

info.description: Titles in the user's Scryer media library: films, series and anime, by facet, words in the title and whether they are monitored, a page at a time (limit, offset), with each one's library, status and episodes on disk.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

facet.description: `movie`, `series` or `anime`; every facet when left out.

limit.description: At most this many titles (default 50, at most 300).

offset.description: Titles to skip, for the next page.

info.name: scryer_library
info.title: Browse the Scryer library

tools.does: Look up films, series and anime to add to Scryer

annotations.title: Look up titles to add to Scryer

info.description: Searches Scryer's metadata for films, series and anime by title (one facet, or all): each result's ids (tvdbId, tmdbId, imdbId) for scryer_add, and whether it is in the library already.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

facet.description: `movie`, `series` or `anime`; every facet when left out.

limit.description: At most this many results per facet (default 10).

info.name: scryer_search
info.title: Look up titles to add to Scryer

tools.does: See what Scryer is downloading

info.description: What Scryer is downloading: each item's title, progress, status, time left and client, and why one needs the user.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

info.name: scryer_queue
info.title: See Scryer's downloads

tools.does: Add a film, series or anime to Scryer

info.description: Adds a film, series or anime to the user's Scryer library by the ids scryer_search gave (facet and at least one id; give name too so the user sees it), monitored unless told, so Scryer finds and downloads it. A title already in the library is left as it is. The user confirms each call unless the Scryer connection lets you act.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

library.description: A library's name, slug or id; Scryer's default library for the facet when left out.

monitor.description:
A series' or anime's episodes to monitor: `all` (default when monitored), `future`, `missingAndFuture` or
`none`.

monitored.description: Monitor it, so Scryer finds and downloads it (default true).

name.description: Its name, shown to the user before an add (Scryer's metadata names it).

tmdbId.description: The TMDB id (films are mostly known by it).

tvdbId.description: The TVDB id (from `scryer.search`); at least one id is needed.

info.name: scryer_add
info.title: Add to Scryer

tools.does: Find Scryer's settings and operations in its API

info.description: Finds and describes Scryer's GraphQL operations and types, to read or change any of its settings (indexers, download clients, seeding profiles, quality, general settings, jobs): `search` words in names and descriptions; `operation` one query or mutation with its arguments, the input types they take and what it returns; `type` one type's fields. With none, how big the API is.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

operation.description: One query or mutation by name: its arguments, the input types they take, and what it returns.

search.description: Words in operation and type names and descriptions (`indexer`, `download client`, `seeding`).

type.description: One type by name: its fields, input fields or values.

info.name: scryer_schema
info.title: Look up Scryer's API

tools.does: Read anything from Scryer's API (settings, indexers, download clients)

info.description: Runs a GraphQL query on Scryer (a query document and its variables), checked against Scryer's schema first; mutations go through scryer_mutate. Credentials in the answer are redacted, and a long answer is cut (it says where): select fewer fields or page.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

operationName.description: The operation to run, when the document has several.

query.description:
A GraphQL query document (`query { indexers { id name isEnabled } }`): checked against Scryer's schema
first. No mutations or subscriptions.

info.name: scryer_query
info.title: Read from Scryer

tools.does: Change Scryer's settings through its API

info.description: Runs one GraphQL mutation on Scryer: its name, its arguments by name and the fields to read back (its scalar fields when left out), checked against Scryer's schema first. Put a password or API key in as {"$secret": "<connection>"}: PDT fills in that connection's secret, so it never passes through you. The user confirms each call unless the Scryer connection lets you act; deleting, resetting, upgrades and calls that send a secret always ask.

args.description:
Its arguments by name (`{"input": {...}}`). A credential goes in as `{"$secret": "<connection>"}`: PDT puts
that connection's secret there.

connection.description: A Scryer connection's name; the only one when left out.

mutation.description: The mutation's name (`createIndexerConfig`, `updateGeneralSettings`; scryer_schema lists them).

select.description: The fields to read back (`id name isEnabled`); its scalar fields when left out.

info.name: scryer_mutate
info.title: Change Scryer
